title: An agent asks to resize a scratch pane
body:
decade's MCP tools let an agent start a program in a scratch pane (`scratch.open`), capture what it draws (`screenshot`) and record it (`record`). No tool sets the pane's size, so the pane is whatever size the layout gives it. A README recording needs a set size: a GIF about twice as wide in pixels as GitHub shows it, with the terminal inside at a set number of columns and rows. Today the person drags the pane by eye while the agent reads the size back.

## Proposal

- An MCP tool `scratch.resize` takes a scratch pane's name and a width and height in pixels.
- decade asks the person every time. Unlike `screenshot` and `record`, no pane mode lets a resize through without asking.
- The answer gives the size the pane ended up with, which can differ from the request when the layout cannot fit it.

## Open

- How the layout makes room: by shrinking the neighbouring panes, by floating the pane, or by refusing a size that does not fit.
- Whether the pane goes back to its old size when its program exits, or only when an agent asks.
close_reason: Landed in 4392ac1: the MCP tool scratch.resize asks every time, moves the pane's borders with Layout::resize_to and answers with the size reached. The note above lists the choices the issue left open.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/3cd5690e
notes.text: Jack decided the open points: decade moves the pane's split borders to get as close to the requested size as the layout allows, taking room from neighbouring panes, and the answer gives the size reached. The pane keeps that size until someone resizes it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/3cd5690e
notes.text:
Choices the round made that the issue and Jack's note left open, in 4392ac1:

- The size is the pane's client area, the pixels a `screenshot` of the pane has. decade rounds each side to the nearest whole cell of its grid, since panes move in cells. A request of 640x400 at 9-pixel cells reaches 639x400.
- Along each axis decade moves the border after the pane first, then the border before it. It takes room from the nearest pane first and then from panes further out, each down to `MIN_PANE`, 4 cells.
- A shrinking pane gives its room to the pane after it, or to the one before it when nothing follows.
- The dialog offers only Allow (y) and Deny (n).
- decade refuses a tab with a zoomed pane, and a width or height of 0.
